## GroupUtils namespace

Make-side helpers for Midnight offer groups.

Groups sit between `Offer.create` and `Tree.create`<!-- -->: they assign a content-addressed group id to offers that share one consumption bucket. One group must use one cap mode and value because Midnight tracks a single consumed scalar per maker and group. Tree helpers derive that id for explicit groups and preserve it on grouped offer copies.

[hash(offers)](./midnight-sdk.grouputils.hash.md)


</td><td>

Derives the deterministic content-addressed id for a group of offers.

This mirrors the router implementation: hash each offer with `group = 0`<!-- -->, sort those hashes, concatenate them, then keccak the result.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[isGroupInput(entry)](./midnight-sdk.grouputils.isgroupinput.md)


</td><td>

Returns whether an entry is an explicit group rather than a standalone offer.

Plain offer objects can also contain incidental `offers` properties, so the discriminant must reject values that still carry the offer `market` field.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[toStructs(group)](./midnight-sdk.grouputils.tostructs.md)


</td><td>

Converts a group into ABI-compatible offers carrying the derived group id.

Use after `Group.create` for custom encoders that need offer structs with their final group id. The id is derived from the full offer list and applied while encoding, so plain groups cannot drift from offer fields.

This helper is encode-only and does not validate protocol group mechanics. Validate with `Group.create` or [OfferUtils.validateOfferGroup()](./midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateoffergroup.md) before relying on the output for signing, tree roots, or calldata.


</td></tr>
